header.sector: AI model developers and AI platforms / applications
header.title: Labs can silently cut subscription value by not raising limits after price cuts

s01_bottom_line.text: Both OpenAI and Anthropic cut API token prices but did not fully raise subscription token limits in step, so API-equivalent subscription value fell without the headline price changing; tracking these shifts is a research opportunity for modeling lab economics. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
The article argues you need to re-check per-plan/model/token costs continuously to accurately model AI lab financials. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Because subscription value can drift silently, analysts modeling AI-lab subscription revenue and margins must track real-time (plan, model, token) limits rather than headline prices.

items.text: OpenAI didn't change Sol token limits when releasing 6.1 Sol, causing API-equivalent value to drop ~30% ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Anthropic's ~20% token increase for Max plans and ~50% for Pro plan didn't fully offset the Opus 5.5 API price cut ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Anthropic did not increase Fable token limits with the 5.1 release but did increase Opus token limits with the 5.5 price cut.

s04_key_evidence.label: API-equivalent value drop
s04_key_evidence.quote: We already showed earlier that OpenAI didn’t change Sol token limits on the $200/month plan when they released 6.1 Sol. This caused the API-equivalent value to drop ~30%.

s04_key_evidence.label: token limit adjustment after price cut
s04_key_evidence.quote: Anthropic also didn’t increase Fable token limits at all with the release of 5.1, but they did up Opus token limits with the 5.5 price cut.
